what: The line said `43.66 freed: kept, or purged and still counted`, which reads as if purged pages were charged to the limit. They are not: admission and the releases read the system's footprint (VmRSS on Linux, phys_footprint on macOS), and the number in the line is mimalloc's committed count less the live heap, a count that never falls on a purge. From that log alone nobody can say how much a purge would have returned.
cost: a wrong lead in the task brief (the limit was not charged with purged memory); time reading the allocator to rule it out
cause: a number that is an upper bound printed with words that say what it might be, not what it is
whys: why wrong: the line's words offered two readings and one of them is a bug that does not exist
why possible: mimalloc keeps no count that falls on a purge, and the line printed the one it has
why not caught: the next clause (`at most N of it freed and resident`) has the real bound, after the misleading one
property: a derived number shown without saying it is a bound and that nothing decides on it
class: a log line that suggests a cause it cannot show
prevention: the line now says `not live: kept freed, or purged; this count never falls on a purge and nothing is charged by it`; every give-back and purge is a span with the footprint before and after, which `blaze explain memory` lists (memory_give_backs)
workaround: read `at most N of it freed and resident` and the `memory purge` spans' `returned`
fix: daemon.rs MemoryLine and its test (written, not compiled)
state: written on int-1112, not compiled or run
